## Overview

The `data_frame_factor` specification describes an on-disk representation of a data frame factor,
i.e., a factor-like object where the levels are the rows of a data frame (or any data frame-like object).
This is based on the `DataFrameFactor` class from the [**S4Vectors** Bioconductor package](https://bioconductor.org/packages/S4Vectors).

## Object metadata

The `OBJECT` file should contain a `data_frame_factor` property, itself a JSON object with the following properties:

- `version`, a string specifying the version of the `data_frame_factor` format.
```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
cat("  This should be set to \"", as.character(.version), "\".", sep="")
```

## Directory structure

### Contents

The directory should contain:

- `OBJECT`, a JSON file as described above.
- `contents.h5`, a HDF5 file.
- `levels/`, a subdirectory.

Optionally, it may also contain:

- `element_annotations/`, a subdirectory.
- `other_annotations/`, a subdirectory.

### `contents.h5`

This should contain an `data_frame_factor` group.

The `data_frame_factor` group should contain `codes`, a 1-dimensional dataset containing the factor codes. 
The datatype of this dataset should be representable by a 64-bit unsigned integer.
Each entry corresponds to an element of the data frame factor and contains a row index into the `levels/` object.
Values of this dataset should be less than the number of levels, i.e., height of the `levels/` object.

Unlike the codes for [`string_factor`](../string_factor), missing values are not currently supported for `data_frame_factor/codes`.

Optionally, the `data_frame_factor` group may contain `names`, a 1-dimensional string dataset of the same length as `codes`.
This contains the name for each element of the data frame factor.

### `levels/`

The `concatenated/` subdirectory contains a child object that satisfies the `DATA_FRAME` interface.
The height (i.e., number of rows) in this child object defines the number of levels in the data frame factor.

It is recommended that the rows of the `levels/` object are not duplicated. 
This is not strictly required but downstream applications may assume unique levels in a factor-like object.

### `element_annotations/`

The `element_annotations/` subdirectory contains a child object that satisfies the `DATA_FRAME` interface.
The child object should have number of rows equal to the length of the `data_frame_factor/codes` dataset.
Each row corresponds to an entry of the data frame factor and contains additional annotations for that entry.

If this subdirectory is absent, no additional annotations are available for elements of the data frame factor.

### `other_annotations/`

The `other_annotations/` subdirectory contains a child object that satisfies the `SIMPLE_LIST` interface.
The child object holds extra annotations for the entire data frame factor.

If this subdirectory is absent, no extra annotations are available for the data frame factor.

## Height

The height of a data frame factor is defined as the length of the `data_frame_factor/codes` dataset in `contents.h5`.
